## The symptom

A two-machine federation probe writes a row on frame A, polls frame B, and reports:

```
=== VERDICT forward=1 reverse=0 ===
```

One direction works, the other reads 0. That asymmetry looks exactly like a
half-open data path, so the investigation goes to the transport layer:
holepunch, DHT universe, relayed-vs-direct paths, socket churn.

On WI-6209 that reflex was **right once and wrong twice**. There genuinely was a
transport bug (two VMs running different bundles — one lacked the
`samePrivateIPv4Subnet24` holepunch fix, so the leg *it* dialled never came up).
But after that was fixed and verified — `never_came_up=0` on both frames, direct
non-relayed paths, channels open — the reverse leg *still* read 0. That surviving
0 was not a second defect. It was the probe writing to a tuple that publishes
nothing.

## Why the write goes nowhere, silently

**A pot has one identity but two local names.** `harness_shared.pots.public_key`
is byte-identical on every frame in the pot. `(workspace_id, pot_home_slug)` is
**local to each machine**:

| frame | workspace_id | pot_home_slug |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fed-a | `workspace-319be5e5` | `spoon-knife-pot` |
| fed-b | `workspace-b31a7a01` | `octocat-spoon-knife` |

So a probe that resolves the workspace on one frame and reuses it on the other —

```bash
# WRONG: WS is resolved on fed-a…
WS="$(sql a "SELECT workspace_id FROM harness_shared.pot_members
             WHERE coalesce(origin,'local')='local' ORDER BY joined_at LIMIT 1;")"
# …then written on BOTH frames
write_row a "$WS" "$FWD"   # fine, it is A's own workspace
write_row b "$WS" "$REV"   # lands in a tuple fed-b has never booted
```

— writes the reverse row into `workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife` **on fed-b**, a
`(workspace_id, harness_slug)` fed-b does not have booted. No substrate binding
owns it, so nothing ever drains it. The row sits in the table forever as
`origin='local'` and the poll on A reads a clean, confident `0`.

**And it does not even error.** `assert_work_item_pot_membership` rejects a
made-up harness slug — but only after this guard:

```sql
-- Fail OPEN for a workspace with no platform Pot (isolated fixtures / un-potted tenant).
v_platform := harness_shared.workspace_platform_pot(NEW.workspace_id);
IF v_platform IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;
```

An unknown workspace has no platform pot, so the trigger **fails open** and
accepts the row. The one case that most needs rejecting is the one waved
through. (Write the same bogus slug under a workspace that *does* have a platform
pot and you get a loud rejection — which is how the trap was finally noticed.)

## The discriminator: `substrate_outbox.drained_at`

A local write destined to federate is captured into
`harness_shared.substrate_outbox` and later drained to a peer log. One query
separates the two causes:

```sql
SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug,
       (drained_at     IS NOT NULL) AS drained,
       (quarantined_at IS NOT NULL) AS quarantined
FROM harness_shared.substrate_outbox
WHERE key = '<the feature_id you wrote>';
```

Measured on the live rig, this cleanly split the probes:

| probe | tuple written | drained | reality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `F-6209-REV-…` | `workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife` on **B** | `f` | mis-targeted — never publishable |
| `F-6209-REVTRUE-…` | `workspace-b31a7a01/octocat-spoon-knife` | `t` | arrived on A in **6s** |
| `F-6209-SK-REV-…` | `workspace-b31a7a01/spoon-knife` | `t` | arrived on A, but **after 90s** |

Read it as:

- **no outbox row** → the capture trigger never fired; the INSERT targeted
  something not federated at all.
- **row, `drained_at IS NULL`** → your write is mis-targeted. No booted binding
  owns that `(workspace_id, harness_slug)` on that frame. **A test bug, not a
  replication failure.**
- **row, `drained_at` set, still unarrived** → a genuine replication/transport
  failure *or* a poll window that expired too early.
- **`quarantined_at` set** → the substrate refused to publish it.

## The second false negative: a poll window shorter than a healthy delivery

`fed_merge_assert` defaults to `tries=30` at 3s — exactly 90 seconds. On the
repaired rig one legitimate reverse write landed **after** that window closed:
the probe reported `0`, and the row was sitting on the destination
`origin='remote'` minutes later. A healthy link can exceed 90s. Treat a bare
timeout as "not yet observed", never as "did not replicate" — check
`drained_at` before concluding anything.

## Do this instead

1. **Resolve each frame's own scope.** Pair frames by
   `harness_shared.pots.public_key`; never copy a `workspace_id` or a
   `pot_home_slug` across machines. Resolve the write target on the frame you are
   about to write to.
2. **Poll destination-side slug-agnostically.** Federation may remap
   `harness_slug` across peers, so match on `feature_id AND origin='remote'`
   rather than pinning the source slug (`fed_hive_merge_probe` already does).
3. **On a negative, diagnose before you blame the wire.** `fed_diagnose_unmerged
   <frame> <key>` in `bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh` runs the query above and
   prints which class it is. It is wired into the failure path of
   `fed_merge_assert` and `fed_hive_merge_probe`, so a bare `0` no longer reaches
   a human undiagnosed.

## A trap inside the trap

The first cut of `fed_diagnose_unmerged` built its verdict from
`(drained_at IS NOT NULL)` concatenated into a text column and compared the
result against `'t'`. That is wrong: `boolean || text` casts through
`boolean::text`, which renders **`true`/`false`** — psql's `t`/`f` is a *display*
convention of the table formatter, not the value. The guard therefore
misclassified every row.

The fixture test did not catch it, because the fixtures had been hand-written
with the same wrong assumption (`…|t|f`) and passed happily. Only running the
guard against the live database exposed it. The fix was to stop depending on
boolean rendering at all:

```sql
CASE WHEN drained_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END
```

**A fixture you authored from your own mental model tests your model, not the
system.** When a guard parses real output, pin at least one assertion to bytes
the real source produced.
